question: Can a social security agreement help me qualify for a Canadian pension if I spent part of my working life abroad?
generated_answer:
You may qualify for a full Canadian pension even if you have worked only in Canada. You can also combine your periods of contribution or periods of residence in a social security agreement country with your periods of contribution to the Canada Pension Plan in order to meet the minimum eligibility requirements. However, if you do not meet the minimum eligibility requirements of the Canada Pension Plan, you may still qualify for a partial pension. Note: If you have not contributed to the Canada Pension Plan and have never worked in Canada, you will not be eligible for a Canadian pension based on your Canadian and foreign periods of contribution or periods of residence.
